key_insight: A deep learning surrogate can replace expensive CPFE simulations to optimize polycrystalline copper microstructures for competing spall and yield strength targets while preserving full-field dynamic response information.
engineering_relevance: This enables rapid, physics-informed microstructure design for solid mechanics problems where both quasi-static and impact performance must be balanced.
method: 3D U-Net maps 3D microstructure geometry to full-field velocity histories from plate-impact simulations.
Stochastic microstructure generation plus derivative-free optimization explores candidate designs efficiently.
A distribution-consistent reliability region (DCRR) uses MMD to flag surrogate predictions that drift beyond the training distribution.
evidence_signal: Across multiple optimization cases, CPFE validation showed less than 3% prediction error, and surrogate-driven optimization cut cumulative evaluation time by about four orders of magnitude.
watch_item: Reliability depends on staying within a well-covered training distribution, so distribution shift during optimization must be monitored carefully.
paper_title: Deep learning driven framework for optimization of polycrystalline microstructures under competing strength requirements
